name: Jeu de Paume
known: It is a non-profit association under the 1901 law, chaired by Alain Dominique Perrin and directed by Quentin Bajac (Jeu de Paume website).

name: Le Bal
known: Co-founded by photographer Raymond Depardon and Diane Dufour, its director.

name: Louvre
known: Runs Louvre-Lens, the Conservation Centre and the Delacroix museum, lends to Louvre Abu Dhabi, and partners with the Petit Palais in Avignon and Musée Bonnat in Bayonne.

name: Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature
known: Founded by François and Jacqueline Sommer.
The foundation carries the founder's name.
It supports the museum's acquisitions, loans, and preventive conservation and restoration (museum website).

Claude d'Anthenaise, the museum's director, said the foundation once ran like a private hunting club, that a president who was a former banker restored its finances, and that attendance rose from about 7,000 family visitors a year to over 120,000 (Académie des Beaux-Arts interview, 2019).
Neither the museum nor Fondation François Sommer posts annual reports, accounts, a donor list or its board; only the Friends association names its own directors.

name: Palais de Tokyo
known: Guillaume Désanges has been director since 2022 (Wikipedia).
Its director is named by the government or city.

name: Palais de la Porte Dorée (Musée national de l'histoire de l'immigration)
Paris Musées (Réseau des Musées de la Ville de Paris)
known: Delphine Levy, who led the reform project, was named chief executive and Anne Hidalgo became chair of the board (English Wikipedia).
Anne-Sophie de Gasquet was Director General in April 2023 (The Art Newspaper edition France, Philippe Régnier, 14 April 2023).

City of Paris subsidy: about 55 million euros, stable in 2023 compared with 2022 (Director General Anne-Sophie de Gasquet, interviewed by Philippe Régnier, "Anne-Sophie de Gasquet : À Paris Musées, un vrai engagement dans le domaine du développement durable", The Art Newspaper edition France, 14 Apr

name: Pinault Collection (Bourse de Commerce)
known: Privately endowed by the founder of the Kering luxury group.

name: Le Confort Moderne
known: Opened on 20 May 1985, founded by Françoise Bordage, Yorrick Benoist, Francis Falceto and Philippe Auvin.

name: Cap Moderne (Villa E-1027 and Le Cabanon)
known: The Conservatoire du littoral owns the site (press release, Association Cap Moderne) and bought the villa in 1999 (partners page, in French).
Public bodies named: Ministry of Culture through DRAC PACA, Conservatoire du littoral, PACA Region, Alpes-Maritimes department, with logistics from the town.
Site owned by the Conservatoire du littoral and managed by the Centre des monuments nationaux since 2018.
Eileen Gray's 1929 villa and Le Corbusier's Cabanon stand on a site owned by the Conservatoire du littoral.

name: CEAAC
known: The Ministry of Culture announced on 1 July 2024 that it awarded the centre the label "centre d'art contemporain d'intérêt national" and names Alice Motard as its director.

The building is the former Neunreiter store: Eugène Neunreiter, founder in 1865 of the glassware and porcelain firm of that name, bought the property in 1878 and set up a sales shop, warehouses and housing.

name: Le Fresnoy - Studio national des arts contemporains
Pictanovo
known: Its president is Grégory Tempremant and its managing director is Godefroy Vujicic (Pictanovo site).
